newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA STOCKS - factors to watch - June 20.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA STOCKS - factors to watch - June 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Malaysian stocks on Friday:

* Composite Index of blue chips gained 9.36 points to 1,097.48 on Thursday, while Second Board slipped 3.07 to 578.16, as momentum shifted back to main liners. Blue chip index may test 1,100 before week-end.

* National car-maker Proton and parent company Hicom set to release results for year to March 31, 1997 after market closes. Analysts see Proton net at 713 million ringgit versus 354 million a year ago. Hicom net seen rising to 571.8 million ringgit from 284.5 million.
* Stocks will probably gain further, said the head of research at a local brokerage firm. But he said the activity is mainly from locals, not foreigners.
"I don't think foreigners have come in, in a big way. My hunch is it's local institutions. Syndicate funds are very active and back into action," he said.
* Thailand's economic problems, including the sinking of its baht to a 12-year low, had so far not spilled over to affect Malaysian sentiment, analysts said.
* Elsewhere, on Wall Street, the Dow broke a three-day losing run, ending up 58.35 points to 7777.06 on Thursday.
* Among local stocks in the news, Malaysia Airlines said it expects to issue five-year bonds with detachable warrants to raise 1.5 billion ringgit.
* Construction firm Esprit Group Bhd, whose stock has been suspended, said it is entering into a joint venture to develop an Indonesian toll road.

* Len Cheong Holding Bhd, a maker of wooden furniture and rubberwood products, is set to list on the Second Board at an offer price of 2.00 ringgit. It has 2.38 million shares in its public issue and is also offering 3.68 million shares for sale.
